 The imagery which I have employed will be found, in many instances, to have been
drawn from the operations of the human mind, or from those external actions by which
35 they are expressed. This is unusual in modern poetry, although Dante and Shakespeare are
full of instances of the same kind: Dante indeed more than any other poet, and with greater
success. But the Greek poets, as writers to whom no resource of awakening the sympathy
of their contemporaries was unknown, were in the habitual use of this power; and it is the
study of their works (since a higher merit would probably be denied me), to which I am
40 willing that my readers should impute this singularity.
